title: Chapter 1.  Formation & Identity of the Union Territory

blocks.content: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (DNH&DD) is one of India's youngest Union Territories in its present form, created by MERGING two previously separate UTs on 26 January 2020. This merger event, its legal instrument, and the territory's unusual two-part, non-contiguous geography are the single highest-yield facts in this entire subject — expect at least one direct question on the merger date and reason in almost any exam covering this UT.
The 2020 Merger — What Was Merged and Why

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Union Territory's identity was reshaped by the major merger implemented in 2020.
The territory is unique for being geographically divided into three separated pieces.
Administrative unification aims to streamline governance and resources across the regions.

blocks.content: Before 2020, India had two separate, small Union Territories on the west coast: 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli' (a single enclave bordering Gujarat and Maharashtra) and 'Daman and Diu' (two small coastal enclaves, physically separated from each other, both surrounded by Gujarat).

The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019, passed by Parliament, merged these two UTs into a single new Union Territory named 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu', effective from 26 January 2020 — deliberately chosen to coincide with Republic Day.

The stated official rationale was administrative efficiency and cost-saving: the two erstwhile UTs, despite being geographically distant from each other, shared broadly similar colonial (Portuguese) histories, overlapping administrative cadres, and had separate secretariats and budgets that the Government of India judged could be consolidated into one unified administration.

This makes DNH&DD unique in having been created via a MERGER of two existing UTs, rather than by carving territory out of a state (like Chandigarh) or through direct annexation and international treaty (like Puducherry) — an important distinguishing fact for polity/current-affairs comparison questions.

cells: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (DNH&DD)
Dadra and Nagar Haveli (UT since 1961) + Daman and Diu (UT since 1987)
The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019
2 — one for Dadra & Nagar Haveli (ST-reserved) and one for Daman & Diu (unreserved)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: 'DNH&DD was formed by MERGING two UTs, not by splitting a state' — the exact opposite process from how Telangana or Uttarakhand were created. This single distinction is one of the most reliably tested facts about this territory.
A Territory in Three Separated Pieces

Unlike almost any other Indian state or UT, DNH&DD does not form one continuous landmass. It consists of THREE physically separate, non-contiguous enclaves, all completely surrounded by neighbouring states, and none of them touching each other directly.

cells: Inland enclave between Gujarat and Maharashtra; Dadra is a small pocket close to Gujarat's Vapi area, while Nagar Haveli is the larger surrounding block, straddling the Gujarat–Maharashtra border
Coastal enclave on the Arabian Sea coast, entirely surrounded by Gujarat (Valsad district), roughly 30 km from Dadra & Nagar Haveli's Silvassa

A small island (plus a small mainland strip, Ghoghla) off the southern tip of Gujarat's Saurashtra/Kathiawar peninsula (near Una, Gujarat), several hundred kilometres from Daman and from Dadra & Nagar Haveli by road

items: Remember the year 2020 as the critical timeline for the Union Territory merger.
Note the geographic configuration of the UT existing in three non-contiguous segments.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Diu is physically an ISLAND (connected to the mainland strip of Ghoghla by a bridge), separated from the Kathiawar coast of Gujarat by a creek — a frequently tested geographical detail that distinguishes it from Daman, which sits directly on the mainland coast.

items: DNH&DD formed 26 January 2020 by merging Dadra & Nagar Haveli (UT since 1961) and Daman & Diu (UT since 1987), via the Merger of Union Territories Act, 2019.
Capital: Daman. Largest town: Silvassa. 3 districts: Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman, Diu.
The UT is non-contiguous — three separate enclaves surrounded by Gujarat and Maharashtra, none touching each other.
Diu is an island (linked to Ghoghla on the mainland by a bridge); Daman sits directly on the mainland coast.
2 Lok Sabha seats: Dadra & Nagar Haveli (ST-reserved) and Daman & Diu (unreserved).
